title: Cross-environment escalation liaison and emergency rollback coordination
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported generation regressions after a rolling model rollout (model:v3.1 -> model:v3.2-quant). Failures surfaced as: increased hallucinations on specific prompt families, tokenization mismatches for on-prem customers using pinned tokenizer bundles, and elevated tail latency during canary windows.

Goal: Create a single-source playbook and an assigned escalation liaison to coordinate emergency rollbacks, cross-environment fixes (hotfixes, KV cache invalidation, tokenizer re-sync), and customer communication. The playbook must include decision criteria for full rollback vs. targeted mitigation, artifact locations, and per-environment steps (Hosted, Dedicated, Private/VPC).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Liaison assigned and on-call rotation added to oncall schedule.
2) Playbook validated with a tabletop run with Eng/Reliability/SE teams.
3) A rollback performed in staging using the documented steps and validated against the regression test suite.
4) Communication templates for customers and account teams available.
5) Postmortem template ready with timeline and root-cause checklist.
rollback_playbook_summary:
- Decision gates: customer-facing errors OR >2% regression in quality evals on pinned prompts OR sustained tail-latency breaches for >5 minutes -> immediate rollback.
- Hotpath: Hosted -> model routing config rollback + cache flush.
- Dedicated -> capacity pool switch to previous image + rolling restart with zero-downtime flag.
- Private/VPC -> ship orchestrator rollback bundle and remote upgrade script (with signed artifacts) and coordinate with customer's infra contact.
- Tokenizer mismatch detection: compare model.tokenizer_hash with deployed_tokenizer_hash; if mismatch, prefer tokenizer rollback over model if tokenizer bundle was unpinned.
observability_checklist:
- Metrics: per-model accuracy/regression eval dashboard, per-tenant token error rates, 95/99/999 latency, queue_depth, gpu_saturation.
- Traces: sample slow requests and attach KV cache hit rate.
- Logs: request_id, model_version, tokenizer_hash, execution_kernels used.
- Dashboards/links: https://dashboard.redwood.company/models/regressions, https://observability.redwood.company/trace/search?tag=rollback_test
steps:
1) Triage: collect 3 reproducing prompts and attach production request IDs.
2) Hotfix attempt (if low-risk): adjust routing weight to a compatible variant (e.g., v3.2-quant -> v3.1-int8) and monitor 15 mins.
3) If regression persists: engage liaison, notify affected accounts via standard template, and schedule rollback window.
4) Execute rollback: update routing config (hosted), coordinate Dedicated ops to switch GPU pool image, and for Private deliver signed rollback bundle + runbook for customer infra.
5) Validate: run regression eval suite and smoke tests, confirm latency and quality metrics normalized.
6) Post-incident: collect artifacts, escalate to Research for root cause of quality degradation.
communication_plan:
- Immediate: send templated high-priority notification to affected customers with expected mitigation ETA. Template link: https://confluence.redwood.company/incident-templates/rollback.
- Internal: open #inc-rollback Slack channel, invite PMs, SEs, and account owners.
- Post-incident: personalized follow-up with affected accounts summarizing cause, fix, and remediation steps (including optional credits).
logs_and_artifacts:
- Example failing requests: req-20260312-87a3 (hosted), req-20260312-9f21 (dedicated), req-20260312-cc55 (private).
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 (rollback helper), https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/88 (cache-flush-tool).
- Artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/rollbacks/ENG-12047/v3.1-vs-v3.2-eval.tar.gz
- Playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.company/incident/ENG-12047-playbook
notes:
- Private deployments require signed bundles; coordinate with security for HSM signing if customer enforces it.
- Some Dedicated clusters use pinned CUDA kernels; rolling back may necessitate a kernel fallback plan (ENG-11750 dependency).
- KV cache invalidation patterns differ: Hosted supports prefix invalidation API, Dedicated uses RPC to agent, Private may require customer-run script. Provide all three variations in the runbook.
- Ensure PMs add impacted customers to postmortem invite list.
